slides.heading: Merge Linked Lists
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Merge Linked Lists, a hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Merge two sorted lists in place; return the head of the merged list.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Merge two sorted lists in place; return the head of the merged list.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Walk both sorted lists, splicing the smaller node in front each time, without new nodes.
slides.narration: Walk both sorted lists, splicing the smaller node in front each time, without new nodes.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Copy into an array, sort, rebuild → O((n+m) log)
Iterative merge with a dummy head → O(n+m), O(1)
slides.narration: Copying everything and sorting ignores that both lists are sorted. A merge with a dummy head relinks nodes in linear time and constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Keep pointers into both lists and a previous pointer
slides.narration: Step by step. First, keep pointers into both lists and a previous pointer. Second, splice the smaller node. Third, attach any leftover tail. Fourth, return the smaller head.
